text:
nidhi: FYI staging p99 token latency jumped ~30% after the q8-onboard merge (PR 4829). Noticed around 18:12 UTC.

sam: saw the alert too, thanks. Is this the new tokenizer mapping change?

leo: can reproduce locally with the new checkpoint + q8 flags. Short sequences spike.

maya: stack from perf-runner: `model:onboard/q8-checkpoint` shows kernels switching to fallback mid-stream. Might be kernel selection misroute.

patrick: confirm: fallback to slow kernel often happens after token 128, which wasn't a hot path before. Any kernel selection logs?

deploy-bot: Deploy 4829 completed by @nidhi at 2026-03-17T18:05:12Z. No rollout errors.

nidhi: attaching quick profile snippet, we see continuous batching metric drop and KV hits dropoff at the same time the kernel switches:

```
# perf-sample (trimmed)
seq_len distribution: median=42 p90=130 p99=310
kernel_selected: fast_attn (0-127) -> fallback_attn (>=128)
kv_cache_hit_rate: 0.92 -> 0.64 around token 128
batch_size_mean: 8 -> 3 post-switch
```

sam: kv hit drop smells like tokenizer produced different tokenization for same prefix, causing cache key mismatch? Did vocab or special token mapping change?

leo: tokenizer diffs show new `</s>` handling: previously was a single byte token, new checkpoint maps rare punctuation to extra tokens for short sequences. That could shift offsets and invalidate prefix keys.

maya: ok that explains KV miss. But why kernel selection flips? The runtime chooses kernel based on observed active sequence length and memory plan; if KV entries missing we re-materialize and memory pressure grows -> triggers fallback kernel path.

patrick: action items: 1) revert PR 4829 from staging (temporary) 2) run tokenizer-diff shim to run old tokenizer in front of new model to confirm root cause 3) add unit test to ensure prefix KV stability across tokenizer changes

nidhi: started rollback to previous checkpoint on staging now. ETA ~10m. Will post results.

deploy-bot: Rollback started for deploy 4829 at 2026-03-17T18:25:01Z.

sam: while rollback runs, can someone run a focused bisect to narrow exact tokenizer change? I can help with test harness.

leo: running tokenizer-bisect across tokenizer commits 9a..f3 locally, will post which commit flips kv_hit_rate.

maya: reminder: add logging to kernel-selector so we can correlate selection decisions with kv_hit_rate and batch sizes in future (low overhead counters).

nidhi: rollback complete — staging p99 back to baseline. Confirmed. Will open hotfix PR to restore onboarding but keep old tokenizer mapping until we land KV compatibility shim.

sam: thanks. Please include a small eval against short-seq workloads in the hotfix CI. This only popped because of skewed seq_len distribution.

patrick: noted. I'll file the postmortem blurb and tag eng-runtime and eng-ml. Also flag for release freeze on onboard merges until KV compatibility gating is in place.

leo: bisect result: commit `f1b2c3d` in tokenizer rewriter is the culprit — adds punctuation splitting rule. Test harness shows kv_hit_rate drops to 0.65 immediately. Pushing PR with revert patch now.

nidhi: thanks everyone. Good catch. We'll coordinate a safer shadow rollout for the next checkpoint with the gating checks Maya proposed. :thumbsup:
